calls.body: The Stars are the league’s best for chance quality, but the Blues are near the top at preventing dangerous shots. We’ll side with the Stars.

calls.head: One power play bites, one doesn’t
calls.body: On the power play, Dallas is one of the league’s best, but St. Louis is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Every penalty the Blues take could cost them.

DAL.head: We leaned Dallas’s way (56%), but St. Louis had other ideas.

STL.head: We had St. Louis as slight underdogs (44%), and they pulled it off.

surprises.head: St. Louis got even better looks than usual
surprises.body: St. Louis usually gets some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Even by those standards, this was a night of good looks: a 9.8% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 6.7% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 50 games.

surprises.head: Joel Hofer stole one with a shutout
surprises.body: Hofer stopped all 25 shots, worth 2.8 expected goals. That is more than St. Louis’s winning margin, not counting empty-net goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 40 starts.

story.head: Nothing gets past Hofer
paras: Adam Jiříček played his first NHL game. Mason McTavish made his Blues debut, after five seasons with the Ducks. McTavish struck first for the Blues a minute and a half in. Jake Neighbours and Arttu Hyry squared off early in the second, and Dalibor Dvorský made it 2-0 for the Blues midway through the period. St. Louis had a goal taken off for offside just 58 seconds into the third, but it didn’t cost them in the end. Jimmy Snuggerud added an empty-net goal with less than three minutes left to make it 3-0. Pius Suter added an empty-net goal with just over two minutes left to make it 4-0. Connor McMichael made his Blues debut, after six seasons with the Capitals, and picked up an assist.
The chances were closer than the score. Joel Hofer was perfect for the Blues, 25 saves on 25 shots, and Jake Oettinger stopped 20 of 22.

Brandon Carlo was thrown out with a game misconduct early in the third. Neither power play scored: the Blues killed all four Stars power plays, and the Stars killed all four of St. Louis’. The Blues moved to 1-0-0, tied for first in the NHL in points percentage. The Stars fell to 0-1-0, still last in the NHL.

items.text: It was the first game of the season for both teams, and the Stars lost their home opener.
Two of the preview’s three calls held.
